Unrelated explanation why alcohol makes your head spin: Your inner ear balance organ works by having a little sensor in three rings filled with fluid. When you move, the fluid sloshes around, triggering the sensor. Normally sensor and fluid have the same density, so it is suspended freely. However, when you drink, the sensor absorbs the alcohol faster than the surrounding fluid. Because alcohol has a lower density than water, these sensors start floating upwards, triggering the signal and tricking your inner ear into thinking you're spinning around. After a while, the surrounding fluid absorbs just as much alcohol, normalizing the balance again. The reverse happens the day after, when the sensor is purged of alcohol more quickly and then starts to sink. This makes your head spin the other way around when you close your eyes.
